newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN CABINET APPROVES SHIP REGISTER BILL.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN CABINET APPROVES SHIP REGISTER BILL.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela's cabinet on Wednesday approved a draft Shipping Registration Act clearing the way for the registration of ships leased or partly owned by South Africans.
The Transport Ministry said in a statement the bill would simplify the rules for registration of ships in South Africa, but would retain the requirement for a genuine link.

The draft, which will be considered by a parliamentary committee before it is put to a vote, allows for the registration of ships other than fishing vessels if a majority of the shares are held in South Africa or if it is leased to a South African company.
Fishing vessels will be registered in South Africa only if they are wholly owned by a South African company.
"More ships on the South African register means more South Africans being trained for careers at sea (which) can only be of benefit to the nation as a whole," the ministry said.
The ministry said the government also was investigating existing obstacles to ship financing and the tax environment for shipowners.
Transport Minister Mac Maharaj told a shipping conference in Cape Town last month he favoured a revision of tax rules to help South African shipowners to compete internationally.
"The successfull development of a South African ship register depends on creating a business environment conducive to domestic ship-owning and operating activities.
"To this end and in conjunction with other role players, my department has appointed a consultant to research and make recommendations on the matter of taxation of ship owners," he said.
